scope: The recovered Kotlin harness removes the obsolete output-directory phase guard in deleteLast, updates approved status copy, and adds focused manual-clock loading checks. Twenty test methods cover the implemented status screens, delayed initial/retry progress, fast-request cancellation through recovery, per-attempt reset, quiet background refresh, accessible/stable retry buttons at normal and 2× font sizes, reduced-motion static progress, and deletion. All three status states use their approved Bram artwork.
portabilityChanges: The Gradle init script requires the tool directory supplied by render.sh instead of a machine-specific fallback.
render.sh derives the Android project from its own location and preserves the caller’s configured Java and Android SDK.
Captures, semantics, and the resulting JUnit XML default to the ignored Android build/bram-captures directory; render.sh accepts an optional output-directory argument.
The capture invocation reruns filtered tests so deleting generated output never leaves capture files missing behind an up-to-date test result.
harnessChanges: Removed the output.name == "after" assumption from the existing deleteLast helper so the deletion capture runs with the default build/bram-captures output directory.

Updated existing attention and deletion title assertions to "All good" and the large-text attention body assertion to "Nothing needs your attention right now."; test interactions and behavior coverage remain unchanged.
Updated the existing error-title references in retry and reduced-motion checks to "A little hiccup" without changing retry interactions or loading/failure/recovery assertions at that stage.

Added seven focused loading cases and extended the existing retry failure/success case. Timing uses the manual Compose clock: 199ms grace anchored to pending composition, 200ms deadline, one initial-content frame or up to three nested parent/child display frames, per-frame cancellation checks through recovery using an observable unmerged subtree, and static-pixel comparison for reduced motion. Existing status, deletion, and large-text coverage is preserved.
